key_insight: Group-specific LLM-generated interactions can improve long-tail recommendation accuracy and coverage while constraining overall accuracy loss.
engineering_relevance: Recommendation teams can tune synthetic-data augmentation by item popularity to better serve sparse-interaction items without sacrificing overall ranking quality beyond a chosen threshold.
method: Partition items into groups by interaction frequency.
Optimize LLM-generated interaction augmentation for group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage under an overall NDCG@20 degradation constraint.
Evaluate combined group strategies, LLM scales, and context configurations under token constraints.
evidence_signal: SASRec experiments report group-specific NDCG@20 gains of over 100% and 60% for extreme and regular long-tail items on an industrial dataset, and 40% and 25% on MovieLens-32M, with increased coverage and no significant overall degradation.
watch_item: Individually optimal group strategies are not simply additive, and richer augmentation context increases cost, requiring joint validation and budget-aware tuning.
paper_title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
